OK, let me contribute to this thread.

I think that the misinterpretation of the term FL is this one:

The orange rectangle is a FLAG which has got 2 Flag Limits (FL). What I found is that in a Flag you'll find only one FTR, in this case the FTR is the one marked in lime. And, as you see, it bounced price 2 times:

The FTR is also a FL but there's also the upper flag limit which is represented by the upper side of the orange rectangle. And this is a zone to be watched when approached by a compression or a 3 drives because there are may orders (long in this case) and price could reverse prior to reaching the lower Flag Limit or the FTR. That's why on the first time back to a flag you see the upper and the lower Flag Limits as a Reaction Zone This are only my 2 cents of course, but that's the conclusion I came to by watching how price reacts to zones and where price reacts to!

Please Staurum or Master Harry, correct me if I'm wrong.
IMO, Orange box is the FTR/FL. The difference between these two is that FTR is called FL, once price hit the target. So all the FLs are FTRs. May be Others have different views.

Edge

With my data it lines up perfectly. Also remember once we have the opposing TG hit, that has to be it for that FL, we just cant let it retrace further than advance again, otherwise the kinks would just go forever. Think about it terms of orderflow, breaks the barrier turns back than advances again. the FTR is that very first decision the second its broken. Sometimes it will be small other times they will retrace further prior to hitting TG1.

Also, doesn't it also make sense what looks nice to other traders like where some may draw the FTR (blue), its going to trap them. The more hidden the FL the more powerful it can be:)
